english: Mary and Rose are so familiar with each other. They know exactly when to meet.

english: I wounded a deer. It's bloody.  The leaves get bloodier off in that direction. [The deer leaves a bloody trail on the leaves off in that direction.]
It suddenly turned when a gust of wind hit it.

ojibwe: Indaga niisaakiiwen iwidi adaawewigamigong ji-naadamawiyan ge-agwanenjigeyaan.
english: Why don't you go downhill to the store and get me some snuff.
He helped his son when they fought him.

english: He completed the five-mile course he was told to do.

english: I told you not to hit the dog and you went ahead and hit him anyway.

english: Can you help me cook? You can cook the potatoes.

english: I asked that lady for some potatoes. She only gave me a little bit.

Her snowshoe tracks come from across the river.

ojibwe: Naniizaanendan epizoyan gi... gidoodaabaanens. Mookaagonasowag asiniig.
english: Be careful where you drive your skidoo. The rocks are coming out of the melting snow.
My stew boiled dry. I forgot to fill it back up (with some water).

ojibwe: Mii go zhigwa bapangibiisaag. Mii ganabaj igo ji-ni-gimiwang.
english: Raindrops are falling. I think it's going to start raining.

english: Don't call on him. He only knows bad medicine.
You don't have to call your mum. Give her a surprise visit.
Don't bother your grandfather. He's busy making kinnickinick

Take good care of that token or you might lose it.

The fall before last I made my snowshoes.

ojibwe: Ambe daga da-agwaataawag igiw abinoonjiinyag. Mii go gegaa gabe-ishkwaa-naawakwe zaagagwamowaad imaa nibiikaang.
english: Get those kids out of the water. They've been in the water almost all afternoon.
He fell short jumping up on it.

ojibwe: Awegwen igo odaa-noondawaan aandi eyaanid ininishiban gaa-initaagozid.
english: Anyone can tell it's a mallard duck by its sound.
I wonder who was making that noise outside last night.
They're going to have a big celebration again during the Fourth of July.

english: He found the hole where the gophers live.

ojibwe: Waanda-wiimbaamagad naa 'i waazh imaa nibaad makwa.
english: The den where a bear sleeps is hollow.
My daughter baked some squash.

ojibwe: Aaniin epiitinigozid awe ayaabe gaa-paashkizwad. | Gegaa go niswaak gii-apiitinigozi.
english: How much does the buck you shot weigh? | It weighs almost three hundred pounds.

english: I told him to go hide his car and there it is way out in the open.
A beaver eats by the river.
My mother is still cooking.
I cooked three times today.

ojibwe: Gidaa-wiidookaw ina wii-chiibaakweyaan. Giin gidaa-gabaashimaag igiw opiniig.
english: Can you help me cook? You can cook the potatoes.

I'm waiting for my grandson. He didn't come.

ojibwe: Maazhendaagod gii-noondamaang wewebinidiwaad igiweg noozis miinawaa iniw odikweman.
english: It is sad to hear that my grandson and his wife are getting divorced.
My grandson traded his car.
I can't cash my check.
My son sent me some money.

ojibwe: Gaawiin ganage naa nibizikitaagozisii a'awe akiwenzhiyish aana-ganoonag. Indawaaj niin indookinaa.
english: I tried to call to that old man but he didn't pay any attention to me so I just poked him.
Work with that man working over there.
What's that name of that lady sitting over there.
Reach for that pail over there.

ojibwe: Indaga nawadin awe abinoojiinh; onzaam jiigaya'ii imaa ayaa bagizowining.
english: Grab that child. He's too close to the swimming pool.

ojibwe: Onzaam jiigaya'ii imaa gii-niibawi gaa-onji-nawadidenig ogiboodiyegwaazon.
english: He was standing too close --  that's why his pants caught on fire.

english: What is this needle used for? / This is the one I use for putting beaver hides on hoops.
Don't laugh at how it looks.
He's laughing at his old worn-out moccasins with the holes in them.
He's straightening out his pipe that's sitting there.

ojibwe: Otigwaanining ogii'-inaganaamaan gii-bishigwaganaandang bikwaakwad. Ganabaj ogii-kiiwashkweganaamaan.
english: He hit him in the head when he missed the ball. I think he knocked him unconscious.
